detail.longDescription: The federal government's push to expand Canada's artificial intelligence infrastructure is gaining momentum, with 19 additional companies committing to national principles aimed at ensuring data centre development benefits communities while limiting environmental impacts. The Government of Canada announced Sept. 22 that the new signatories bring the total number of organizations supporting Canada's Responsible Data Centre Development Principles to 42, nearly doubling participation since the initiative launched earlier this month. The framework, introduced Sept. 3, outlines expectations for companies developing data centres across Canada, including protecting electricity customers from additional costs, minimizing water consumption and ensuring projects deliver lasting economic benefits.  googletag.cmd.push(function() { if($(document).width()<900) { s = googletag.defineSlot('/50748803/wco-all-bigbox', [300, 250], 'div-gpt-1632277500385-bbm1'); s.setConfig({targeting: {URL: [window.location.pathname]}}) s.setConfig({targeting: {position: [1632277500385]}}) s.setConfig({targeting: {story_id: 'canadas-data-centre-development-plan-gains-support-from-19-more-companies'}}) s.addService(googletag.pubads()); googletag.pubads().refresh([s], {changeCorrelator: false}); } });  The growing support comes as Canada looks to expand the infrastructure needed to support artificial intelligence, cloud computing and other rapidly developing technologies. Five principles guide development The federal framework establishes five key expectations for companies pursuing data centre projects. Developments are expected to provide lasting benefits to local communities, protect electricity ratepayers, minimize water consumption and environmental impacts, maintain transparency about their effects on surrounding communities and contribute strategic value to Canada's economy. The principles are intended to address concerns surrounding the significant electricity and water requirements associated with large-scale data centres. As demand for AI computing capacity grows, governments and communities are increasingly faced with balancing economic development opportunities against infrastructure capacity and environmental considerations.  googletag.cmd.push(function() { if($(document).width()<900) { s = googletag.defineSlot('/50748803/wco-all-bigbox', [300, 250], 'div-gpt-1632277500385-bbm2'); s.setConfig({targeting: {URL: [window.location.pathname]}}) s.setConfig({targeting: {position: [1632277500385]}}) s.setConfig({targeting: {story_id: 'canadas-data-centre-development-plan-gains-support-from-19-more-companies'}}) s.addService(googletag.pubads()); googletag.pubads().refresh([s], {changeCorrelator: false}); } });  For communities considering future data centre projects, the principles provide a national framework for evaluating potential economic benefits alongside impacts on local resources.  Related Stories:  Ottawa launches national principles for responsible data centre development  Bell’s proposed 1.2-GW Saskatchewan AI hub raises questions over power, public consultation   Major technology companies join initiative Among the 19 new signatories are several major international technology companies, including NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, IBM and Lenovo.  googletag.cmd.push(function() { if($(document).width()<900) { s = googletag.defineSlot('/50748803/wco-all-bigbox', [300, 250], 'div-gpt-1632277500385-bbm3'); s.setConfig({targeting: {URL: [window.location.pathname]}}) s.setConfig({targeting: {position: [1632277500385]}}) s.setConfig({targeting: {story_id: 'canadas-data-centre-development-plan-gains-support-from-19-more-companies'}}) s.addService(googletag.pubads()); googletag.pubads().refresh([s], {changeCorrelator: false}); } });  Other organizations joining the initiative include EllisDon, Energy Storage Canada, Schneider Electric, STACK Infrastructure, Vantage Data Centers and Potentia Renewables Inc. The expanded list also includes Clearway Group of Companies, Enwave Energy Corporation, Global Relay, Kyndryl, OnX, Qu Data Centres, Red Jar Energy Partners and Slate Asset Management. The participating organizations represent a range of industries involved in developing, operating, financing and supplying infrastructure for data centres. Federal officials say the broader participation demonstrates growing industry support for a common approach to expanding Canada's digital infrastructure.
